content:
According to Bloomberg, Apple has raised the monthly and annual fees for AppleCare+ for new Mac and iPad buyers. Here are the details.

AppleCare+ price increase for new iPad and Mac

AppleCare+ is Apple's extended warranty and device protection service, offering additional hardware coverage, technical support, and accidental damage repair.

Bloomberg found that Apple today raised the AppleCare+ monthly fee for Mac and iPad by $0.50 and the annual fee by $5.

In practice, the new charges are as follows:

New Mac lineup

  • Mac mini: $4.99 per month or $49.99 per year
  • Mac Studio: $7.49 per month or $74.99 per year
  • iMac: $7.49 per month or $74.99 per year
  • MacBook Neo: $6.49 per month or $64.99 per year
  • 13-inch MacBook Air: $8.49 per month or $84.99 per year
  • 15-inch MacBook Air: $9.49 per month or $94.99 per year
  • 14-inch MacBook Pro: $11.49 per month or $114.99 per year
  • 16-inch MacBook Pro: $16.49 per month or $164.99 per year
  • Mac Pro: $18.99 per month or $189.99 per year

New iPad lineup

  • iPad and iPad mini: $6.49 per month or $64.99 per year
  • 11-inch iPad Air (M4): $7.49 per month or $74.99 per year
  • 13-inch iPad Air (M4): $8.49 per month or $84.99 per year
  • 11-inch iPad Pro (M5): $11.49 per month or $114.99 per year
  • 13-inch iPad Pro (M5): $12.49 per month or $124.99 per year

It's worth noting that the new charges only affect new Mac and iPad subscribers. Existing customers can still continue using the old prices for now.

As for the multi-device protection plan AppleCare One launched by Apple last year, it does not appear to be affected this time.
